title: Tabitha, arise (Acts 9:32–43)
hook: no eulogy, just a pile of coats held up by the women who wore them
tomorrow: a soldier and a hungry man on a roof. who sent for whom?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a basket down a dark wall, and Barnabas speaking up for Saul. The line: barnabas took him.

At some memorials there's a table: photos, a favorite mug, a jersey, the quilt she made. Objects say who someone was faster than a speech can. Acts tells a story like that. In Joppa lives "a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas," and Acts gives her life one line: "this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did." She falls sick and dies. Her friends lay her in an upper room and send for Peter. When he arrives, nobody gives a speech.
screen: `A TABLE OF THINGS SHE MADE.` → `A DISCIPLE NAMED TABITHA.` → `NOBODY GIVES A SPEECH.`

segments.voice: Today's question: what does a faithful life look like from the outside? Acts answers with clothes. "All the widows stood by him weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them." They don't describe her goodness; they hold it up, stitches you can see. Then Peter sends everyone out, kneels, prays, and says, "Tabitha, arise." "And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up." Jewish tradition answers the same question with clothes too. In the Talmud, a rabbi asks how a person can walk after God, as the Torah commands. His answer: follow God's ways. As God clothed the naked, so you clothe the naked; as God visits the sick, so you visit the sick. And the first example comes from Genesis: "Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them." A coat sewn for someone in need is holy work on both pages. Here's the honest difference. For the rabbis, clothing others is walking in God's own ways, a commandment of the Torah given to the Jewish people. Acts tells Tabitha's story as part of the story of Jesus, and its high point is Peter, praying, calling her back to life. Not the same story. The same kind of coat.
screen: `THE WIDOWS HOLD UP THE COATS.` · `TABITHA, ARISE.` · `THE TALMUD: CLOTHE, AS GOD CLOTHED.` · `SAME KIND OF COAT, DIFFERENT STORY.` · then, large: `FULL OF GOOD WORKS.`

segments.voice: Find one piece of clothing near you: a jacket with a loose button, a sweater you no longer wear. Hold it through the sit and feel the seams, the work someone's hands put into it. Before the bell ends, decide one thing: mend it, or give it to someone who'd wear it.
Tabitha. A disciple of Joppa, also called Dorcas, remembered by the coats she made.
Keep this one: full of good works, the kind you can hold up. Go well.
